ci-price-ramp.slip: It tries pairs from the far end for every start, which is $O(n^2)$ when prices fall.

ci-free-block.slip: It tries every pair of rows and scans the columns, which is right but $O(r^2 c)$.

ci-relay-masts.code:
import heapq

def min_longest_gap(relays, k):
    heap = [-(b - a) for a, b in zip(relays, relays[1:])]
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    for _ in range(k):
        g = -heapq.heappop(heap)
        if g <= 1:
            heapq.heappush(heap, -g)
            break
        heapq.heappush(heap, -(g // 2))
        heapq.heappush(heap, -(g - g // 2))
    return -heap[0]
ci-relay-masts.slip: It halves the longest gap again and again, but splitting a gap evenly into three can beat two halvings.
It lowers the target length one kilometre at a time, which takes up to $10^9$ steps.

ci-ready-blocks.slip: It tries every distinct day in turn, which is $O(n^2)$ when the days differ.

ci-kth-gap.code:
def kth_smallest_gap(positions, k):
    n = len(positions)
    gaps = sorted(abs(positions[i] - positions[j]) for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n))
    return gaps[k - 1]
ci-kth-gap.slip: It lists and sorts every pair, which is $O(n^2 \log n)$.
